Scope: arterial and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, street lighting and telecom networks, sewage pump stations and storm drainage ponds for Phase 1, Part 2 of the 3rd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. At the 27-Oct-2026 data date the project is 77.4% complete against 96.5% planned, 19.1% behind plan, and gained only 0.07% this week against 0.34% planned.

The project is 19.1% behind plan and the current pace cannot close the gap. 22.6% of the work remains with 29 whole weeks left to the contract completion date of 18-May-2027, which needs about 0.78% a week; this week achieved 0.07%. The P6 update (data date 24-Oct-2026) finishes the project on 12-Jun-2027, 25 days late with −24 days of float, while the weekly report still forecasts 18-May-2027. The weakest areas are the Zone 3 networks (66.7% against 98.1% planned), sewage networks in Zones 1 and 3, and the road crossings.

Telecom and sewage are the largest open quantitiesTelecom ducts are 49% installed (31,233 of 64,321 m) and sewer pipes 69% (274 of 396 m). Of the installed network, 2,184 m of potable water, 2,998 m of irrigation and 6,705 m of telecom have been tested and handed to the consultant; no sewer or storm lengths have been handed over yet.

The weekly report forecasts 18-May-2027 with no delay. The water and rainwater milestones of 18-Jan-2026 have passed; the presentation puts the potable water network at 80% and the storm network at 68%.

Procurement of key materials

Share of total quantity delivered to site for the long-lead items. Source: weekly presentation 27-Oct-2026, long-lead items slide.

Pumps: 3 of 15 deliveredGrundfos pump accessories are being installed at the stations, but only 3 pumps have arrived because of global shipping problems. The pump station control panels (IGEC, 1 set) and sewage station panels (WAMCO, 4 sets) are not expected in full until January 2027.
Generators and surge vesselsThe two generators (Kohler – Abunayyan) are in the Kingdom and wait for the factory acceptance test before delivery to site. Surge vessels (7) were due to start arriving around 15-Oct-2026; none is delivered. The water pump maintenance order (SPP) is waiting for parts.

Planned Actual

October head count is 393 (59 staff and 334 labour) against 55 planned. The plan comes from the resource-loaded P6 schedule and is far below the numbers actually on site, so it is not a useful benchmark. Actual labour has fallen from 397 in March–April to 334 in October; the issue log names low manpower and productivity as a cause of delay.

Open issues and risks

IssueOwnerDetail
Pond 4ContractorMODON approved the proposal, but execution is weak. Work starts after the sewer network at the junction of Road 25 and Road 9. Target date 30-Sep-2026 has passed.
Road 25 crossingsContractorAsphalt cutting on Road 25 for the buried networks: the junction with Road 2 is done and the junction with Road 9 is in progress (target 31-Oct-2026). Permits for Road 25 have been stopped.
Pump station equipmentContractorThe water station control system (target 31-Aug-2026, passed), generators, surge vessels and pumps are paid and being manufactured. Water pump maintenance has a purchase order and takes two weeks once parts arrive.
Network testingContractorTesting is needed so complete networks can be handed over. The test plan has been submitted; marked urgent.
Third-party interfacesNot assignedSlab settlement caused by Watco and Al-Issa works; the Al-Issa office gate conflicts with a lighting pole foundation; work in Block F is stopped until the power line to the Chinese factory is extended.
Manpower and productivityContractorLow manpower and equipment and low productivity of the contractor's own crews (MODON issue log, high priority).
Manual excavationContractorExcavation is done by hand because there are no records of the existing services; trial pits are dug before excavation.
Drawings and existing networkContractorIFC drawings do not match site conditions. The BOQ for repairing the existing network is unclear, and the consultant and owner rejected replacing all damaged pipes from manhole to manhole.

Open risks in the MODON register: change in the industrial city's priorities reducing the scope (high), delays in purchases because of regional shipping problems (high), frequent work stoppages lowering daily output (medium), and differences between the signed contract value and the work on site (medium).

Data notes

  • This is the first week uploaded for the project (W01–W03 are empty), so there are no previous-week values: scope quantities have no "This week" figure and the S-curve table has a single row. The weekly progress (+0.07%) is the figure stated in the weekly report.
  • The report week is the contract week stated in the Milestones sheet ("Current Contract Weeks: 75 of 104"), which matches (27-Oct-2026 − 19-May-2025) ÷ 7. The workbook calls itself report #63 and the file names say WPR 56; neither is the week number.
  • Data dates differ between files: weekly report 27-Oct-2026, P6 update 24-Oct-2026, P6 export in the Progress sheet labelled 20-Oct-26, procurement log 20-Oct-2026.
  • Several physical-progress rows in the Weekly Progress Report sheet are wrong: Construction shows 189.8% planned and 206.6% earned; Zone 3 shows 354,449 earned man-hours (the whole project's total) against a 147,160 budget; local roads show 997%; telecom shows 0% and arterial roads 0% although the P6 export records 16,489 and 199 actual man-hours. The P6 export values were used for these rows. The project totals (96.5% planned, 77.4% actual) are consistent with the P6 actual units.
  • The man-hour budget is 458,486 in the total row but 467,288 as the sum of the zones (467,280 in the S-curve sheet).
  • The planned 96.5% to date does not match either curve in the Physical-Chart Data sheet (baseline 92.5%, revised plan 95.2% for October). The chart sheet's monthly actuals stop at June 2026, and the March–May 2026 actuals are identical to the revised plan values.
  • Completion forecasts disagree: weekly report 18-May-2027, P6 update 12-Jun-2027, P6 milestone table 11-Jul-2027, P6 export 24-Oct-2027. Interim milestones 3 to 6 are still marked "F" (forecast) in the weekly report with 2025–2026 dates.
  • The Target schedule sheet and presentation slides 3, 4 and 10 report value-weighted (cost-based) progress labelled as actual or achieved; those figures are not used in this report.
  • Contract value is 233,776,077 SAR in the weekly report and 233,575,734 SAR in the presentation. Invoices: the weekly report shows 37.3M SAR (12 invoices), the invoice log totals 60.6M SAR including the advance payment, and the presentation shows 65.1M SAR disbursed to invoice 14. The invoice log has payment dates for invoices 6–8 that fall before their periods.
  • Manpower: the summary panel shows 388 labour and 57 staff (445), while the monthly table and the presentation show 334 labour and 59 staff (393) for October.
  • Scope quantities: the progress scope slide is labelled "15 September update" and gives telecom as 11,800 of 21,318 and potable water as 2,687 of 2,839, against 31,233 of 64,321 m and 2,687 of 2,992 m on the network quantities slide. The street lighting quantity (53 of 54) has no unit.
  • Procurement: the 20-Oct procurement log shows 2 pumps delivered against 3 in the 27-Oct presentation, labels the Kohler – Abunayyan order as the fuel system (generators in the presentation), and labels the VEGA order as generators (no name in the presentation). The workbook's Procurement sheet has no quantities.
  • The "Modon PM" field in the weekly report is blank; the PM name is taken from the MODON risk and issue log. The Major Quantities sheet shows "Final BOQ submitted and under review" for every network.
